commits.message:
[ssbuffer](feat) Refactor && Protect tcb reuse in some scenario (#3261)

* [ssbuffer](fix) UB usage opt must not move CUBE ops into a VECTOR block

collectRecordChange pulls every transitive dependency of the chain nodes
into the target block. For a chain node that depends on a CUBE op, that
CUBE op was picked up too and had its ssbuffer.block_id rewritten from the
cube block to the VECTOR optBlockId, breaking the CUBE/VECTOR split that
later passes rely on. On a kernel with a matmul feeding VECTOR arithmetic,
the matmul ended up tagged with a VECTOR block_id.

Gate the dependency move on a pure VECTOR_ONLY core type. Read it through
getCoreTypeOfSimpleOpOrCf rather than the graph snapshot, because control
flow ops carry a per-operand comma list ("CUBE, CUBE, ...") on their
attribute while their real core type comes from aggregating the ops inside
their region.

* [ssbuffer](fix) topologically sort block

* init

* unify

* [ssbuffer](fix) Protect tcb reuse in some scenario

* [ssbuffer](fix) Better reorder and loop-carried value planning.

* [ssbuffer](fix) Small VECTOR block without CUBE should come first

* [ssbuffer](fix) while/if keep ssbuffer is outter than mne

+// CHECK: memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 33 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"} : memref<128xf32>

+    %91 = bufferization.to_tensor %alloc_13 restrict writable {ssbuffer.block_id = 32 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"} : memref<128xf32> to tensor<128xf32>
+    %reinterpret_cast_14 = memref.reinterpret_cast %arg9 to offset: [%90], sizes: [128], strides: [1] {ssbuffer.block_id = 32 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"} : memref<?xf32> to memref<128xf32, strided<[1], offset: ?>>

+    %92 = bufferization.to_tensor %alloc_15 restrict writable {ssbuffer.block_id = 32 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"} : memref<128xf32> to tensor<128xf32>

+// RUN: triton-opt --ub-usage-opt %s | FileCheck %s
+
+// A block_id identifies one compute block and a compute block belongs to one
+// core, so a block_id must never be used by both a CUBE and a VECTOR op.
+//
+// The kernel below has CUBE blocks 1/3/4 and VECTOR blocks 5/6/7/8/9/10.
+// UB usage opt moves VECTOR ops between VECTOR blocks to shrink the amount
+// of data crossing a block boundary, and it used to drag a CUBE dependency
+// along into the VECTOR block, leaving that block with both core types.
+// Every block_id below must keep its own core type after the pass.
+//
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @chunk_fwd_kernel_o_npu_kernel
+// CUBE blocks must not gain a VECTOR op.
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 3 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 4 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "VECTOR"
+// VECTOR blocks must not gain a CUBE op.
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 5 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 6 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 7 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 8 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// CHECK-NOT: ssbuffer.block_id = 10 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"
+// The checks above cover everything up to the next positive CHECK.
+// CHECK: return
+func.func @chunk_fwd_kernel_o_npu_kernel(%arg0: memref<?xi8>, %arg1: memref<?xi8>, %arg2: memref<?xbf16> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg3: memref<?xbf16> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg4: memref<?xbf16> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg5: memref<?xbf16> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg6: memref<?xf32> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg7: memref<?xbf16> {tt.tensor_kind = 1 : i32}, %arg8: memref<?xi64> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg9: memref<?xi64> {tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg10: f32, %arg11: i32, %arg12: i32, %arg13: i32, %arg14: i32, %arg15: i32, %arg16: i32, %arg17: i32) attributes {SyncBlockLockArgIdx = 0 : i64, WorkspaceArgIdx = 1 : i64, global_kernel = "local", mix_mode = "mix", parallel_mode = "simd"} {
+  %c32768_i64 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 32768 : i64
+  %c0_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 0 : i32
+  %c4096 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 4096 : index
+  %cst = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 0.000000e+00 : f32
+  %c128 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 128 : index
+  %c256 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 256 : index
+  %c64 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 64 : index
+  %c8192 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 8192 : index

+  %c0 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 0 : index
+  %c32_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 32 : i32
+  %c256_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 256 : i32
+  %c128_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 128 : i32
+  %c32_i64 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.core_type = "CUBE"} 32 : i64

+// RUN: triton-opt --debug-only=memory-effects-tracker --plan-compute-block %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+
+module {
+  // Two views and two reads of one argument must not introduce memory writers.
+  // CHECK-LABEL: Analyzing op func.func @view_reads_have_no_memory_producer
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op %{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}} = memref.load
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Defs:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Preds:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Analyzing op %{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}} = memref.reinterpret_cast
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op %{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}} = memref.load
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Defs:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Preds:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Analyzing op func.return
+  func.func @view_reads_have_no_memory_producer(%arg: memref<?xi32>, %offset: index) -> (i32, i32) {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %lhs = memref.reinterpret_cast %arg to offset: [0], sizes: [4], strides: [1]
+      : memref<?xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    %a = memref.load %lhs[%c0] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    %rhs = memref.reinterpret_cast %arg to offset: [%offset], sizes: [4], strides: [1]
+      : memref<?xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: ?>>
+    %b = memref.load %rhs[%c0] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: ?>>
+    return %a, %b : i32, i32
+  }
+
+  // Defining a new view after a write must preserve the real writer (RAW).
+  // CHECK-LABEL: Analyzing op func.func @view_preserves_raw
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op memref.store %{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}}, %[[RAW_VIEW:[A-Za-z0-9_]+]][
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op %{{[A-Za-z0-9_]+}} = memref.load
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Defs:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] memref.store {{.*}}, %[[RAW_VIEW]][
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Preds:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] memref.store {{.*}}, %[[RAW_VIEW]][
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Analyzing op func.return
+  func.func @view_preserves_raw(%arg: memref<8xi32>, %value: i32) -> i32 {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %c2 = arith.constant 2 : index
+    %lhs = memref.subview %arg[0] [4] [1]
+      : memref<8xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    memref.store %value, %lhs[%c2] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    %rhs = memref.subview %arg[2] [4] [1]
+      : memref<8xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: 2>>
+    %v = memref.load %rhs[%c0] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: 2>>
+    return %v : i32
+  }
+
+  // Defining a view after a read must preserve the reader before a write (WAR).
+  // CHECK-LABEL: Analyzing op func.func @view_preserves_war
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op %[[WAR_READ:[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] = memref.load
+  // CHECK: Analyzing op memref.store
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Defs:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Preds:
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] %[[WAR_READ]] = memref.load
+  // CHECK-NEXT: [memory-effects-tracker] Analyzing op func.return
+  func.func @view_preserves_war(%arg: memref<8xi32>, %value: i32) -> i32 {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %c2 = arith.constant 2 : index
+    %lhs = memref.subview %arg[0] [4] [1]
+      : memref<8xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    %v = memref.load %lhs[%c2] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1]>>
+    %rhs = memref.subview %arg[2] [4] [1]
+      : memref<8xi32> to memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: 2>>
+    memref.store %value, %rhs[%c0] : memref<4xi32, strided<[1], offset: 2>>
+    return %v : i32

+"""Adapt the Ascend compilation stages for a single TLA compilation."""
+import os
+from types import FunctionType, SimpleNamespace
+
+from triton.backends.ascend import compiler as ascend
+from triton.compiler import compiler as triton_compiler
+
+from ._options import _EXTRA_OPTIONS, normalize_extra_options
+
+
+def _bind(fn, **dependencies):
+    # Each invocation gets its own bindings, including concurrent JIT compilations.
+    bound = FunctionType(fn.__code__, {**fn.__globals__, **dependencies}, fn.__name__, fn.__defaults__, fn.__closure__)
+    bound.__kwdefaults__ = fn.__kwdefaults__
+    return bound
+
+
+def _compile_binary(compiler, module, metadata, options):
+    extra = metadata["tla_compiler_args"]
+    if not extra:
+        return compiler(module, metadata, options)
+
+    def command(argv):
+        if os.path.basename(argv[0]) != "bishengir-compile":
+            raise ValueError(f"TLA compiler arguments require bishengir-compile, got {argv[0]!r}")
+        output = argv.index("-o")
+        return [*argv[:output], *extra, *argv[output:]]
+
+    def run(argv, **kwargs):
+        argv[:] = command(argv)
+        return ascend.subprocess.run(argv, **kwargs)
+
+    def join(argv):
+        return ascend.shlex.join(command(argv))
+
+    # The Ascend stages format the debug command and invoke the compiler separately.
+    stage = _bind(compiler, subprocess=SimpleNamespace(**dict(vars(ascend.subprocess), run=run)),
+                  shlex=SimpleNamespace(**dict(vars(ascend.shlex), join=join)))
+    return stage(module, metadata, options)
+
+
+class _TLABackend(ascend.AscendBackend):
+    # The generic reuse handler rebuilds kernels with a plain ASTSource.
+    get_jit_reuse_handler = None
+
+    def parse_options(self, opts):
+        options = super().parse_options(opts)
+        if options.block_batching_factor != 1:
+            raise ValueError("TLA kernels do not support automatic block batching")
+        object.__setattr__(options, "enable_tla_mode", True)
+        object.__setattr__(options, _EXTRA_OPTIONS, normalize_extra_options(opts.get(_EXTRA_OPTIONS, ())))
+        return options
+
+    def add_stages(self, stages, options, language):
+        super().add_stages(stages, options, language)
+
+        def ttadapter(module, metadata):
+            from .compiler import lower_for_backend
+
+            metadata["has_auto_blockify_blacklist_op"] = False
+            metadata["tla_compiler_args"] = lower_for_backend(module, options)
+            ascend._export_profile_metadata(module, metadata)
+            ascend._export_program_grid_metadata(module, metadata)
+            text = ascend._serialize_module(module, options)
+            if options.debug:
+                ascend.get_dump_manager(metadata["hash"]).put(text, "kernel.ttadapter.mlir", binary=False)
+            return text
+
+        compiler = (ascend.linalg_to_bin_enable_npu_compile_910_95
+                    if options.compile_on_910_95 else ascend.linalg_to_bin_enable_npu_compile_A2_A3)
+        stages["ttadapter"] = ttadapter
+        stages["npubin"] = ascend._with_debug_line(
+            lambda module, metadata: _compile_binary(compiler, module, metadata, options), options)
+
+
+def make_backend(target):
+    return _TLABackend(target) if target.backend == "npu" else triton_compiler.make_backend(target)
+
+
+def compile_tla(src, target=None, options=None, _env_vars=None):
+    compile_one = _bind(triton_compiler.compile, make_backend=make_backend)
+    return compile_one(src, target=target, options=options, _env_vars=_env_vars)

+"""Decorators for TLA builtins."""
+
+import warnings
+from functools import wraps
+from inspect import Parameter, signature
+
+
+def experimental(fn):
+    """Emit a UserWarning at the kernel call site when compiling a call to this TLA builtin."""
+    sig = signature(fn)
+    takes_generator = "_generator" in sig.parameters
+
+    @wraps(fn)
+    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
+        generator = kwargs.get("_generator") if takes_generator else kwargs.pop("_generator", None)
+        if generator is not None:
+            warnings.warn_explicit(
+                f"TLA API {fn.__name__} is experimental and may change without notice.",
+                category=UserWarning,
+                filename=generator.file_name,
+                lineno=generator.begin_line + generator.cur_node.lineno,
+                module=generator.jit_fn.__module__,
+                registry=generator.jit_fn.__globals__.setdefault("__warningregistry__", {}),
+            )
+        return fn(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    if not takes_generator:
+        # Request Triton's call-site context while preserving the builtin's other parameters.
+        params = list(sig.parameters.values())
+        index = len(params)
+        if params and params[-1].kind == Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD:
+            index -= 1
+        params.insert(index, Parameter("_generator", Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY, default=None))
+        wrapper.__signature__ = sig.replace(parameters=params)
+    return wrapper

+"""Pipeline lowering, experimental diagnostics and staged copies on A5."""
+import linecache
+

+
+
+@tla.jit
+def staged_copy(X, Y, count, MIX: tl.constexpr, SINGLE: tl.constexpr = False, INVALID: tl.constexpr = ""):
+    limit = 1 if SINGLE else count
+    index = tl.program_id(0)
+    for i in tla.pipeline(limit):
+        if MIX:
+            tile = tla.alloc((16, 16), tl.float16, space="ub")
+            with tla.scope.cube().task("load", stage=0):
+                l1 = tla.alloc((1, 1, 16, 16), tl.float16, space="l1")
+                tla.load_gm_to_l1(tla.view(X + i * 256, (16, 16)), l1)
+                tla.copy_l1_to_ub(l1, tile)
+            with tla.scope.vector().task("store", stage=1):
+                if tla.sub_block_id() == 0:
+                    tla.store_ub_to_gm(tile, tla.view(Y + i * 256, (16, 16)))
+        else:
+            scratch = tla.alloc((2, 64), tl.float32, space="ub")
+            for row in tl.static_range(2):
+                with tla.scope.vector().task("load", stage=0):
+                    tile = tla.subview(scratch, (row, 0), (1, 64))
+                    tla.load_gm_to_ub(tla.view(X + i * 128 + row * 64, (1, 64)), tile)
+            if INVALID == "nested":
+                for j in tl.range(count):
+                    with tla.scope.vector().task("nested", stage=1):
+                        tla.store_ub_to_gm(scratch, tla.view(Y + j * 128, (2, 64)))
+            with tla.scope.vector().task("store", stage=1):
+                tla.store_ub_to_gm(scratch, tla.view(Y + (index + i) * 128, (2, 64)))
+            if INVALID == "carry":
+                index += 1
+            if INVALID == "sync":
+                with tla.scope.vector().task("sync", stage=2):
+                    tla.sync.barrier(tla.sync.PIPE.ALL)
+
+
+def _signature(mix):
+    ptr = "*fp16" if mix else "*fp32"
+    return {"X": ptr, "Y": ptr, "count": "i32"}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mix,single,extra", [
+    (False, False, ()),
+    (True, False, ()),
+    (True, True, ()),
+    (True, False, ("--enable-tla-cv-pipelining=false", )),
+])
+def test_ir(mix, single, extra):
+    ctx = make_context()
+    options = Options()
+    options.npuir_extra_options = extra
+    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="TLA API pipeline is experimental") as caught:
+        module = ast_to_ttir(staged_copy, _signature(mix), {"MIX": mix, "SINGLE": single, "INVALID": ""}, ctx, options)
+    warning, = caught
+    assert warning.filename == __file__
+    assert "for i in tla.pipeline(limit)" in linecache.getline(warning.filename, warning.lineno)
+    # Auto synchronization is required even with no surviving preload stages.
+    features = ascend_ir.get_tla_kernel_features(module)
+    assert features.uses_pipeline
+    assert features.pipeline_preload == (not single and not extra)
+    assert infer_sync_options(features, None, extra) == ()
+    text = str(lower_offline(module, ctx))
+    assert "tla.pipeline" not in text
+    assert text.count("hivm.cv_pipelined_loop") == int(not single and not extra)
+    assert text.count("hivm.preload_num") == (2 if not single and not extra else 0)
+    if mix:
+        assert 'mix_mode = "mix"' in text
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid,message", [("nested", "direct children"), ("carry", "loop-carried values")])
+def test_invalid_pipeline(invalid, message):
+    with pytest.raises(CompilationError, match=message):
+        compile_offline(staged_copy, _signature(False), {"MIX": False, "SINGLE": False, "INVALID": invalid})
+
+
+def test_rejects_handwritten_pipeline_sync():
+    module, _ = compile_offline(staged_copy, _signature(False), {"MIX": False, "SINGLE": False, "INVALID": "sync"})
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="tla.pipeline owns synchronization"):
+        infer_sync_options(ascend_ir.get_tla_kernel_features(module), None, ())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mix", [False, True])
+def test_compile(mix):
+    dtype = torch.float16 if mix else torch.float32
+    size = 256 if mix else 128
+    src = torch.zeros(4 * size, dtype=dtype, device="npu")
+    dst = torch.empty_like(src)
+    kernel = staged_copy.warmup(src, dst, 4, MIX=mix, grid=(1, ))
+    check_kernel_binary(kernel)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mix,single,extra,counts", [
+    (False, False, (), (0, 1, 4)),
+    (True, False, (), (1, 4)),
+    (True, True, (), (1, )),
+    (True, False, ("--enable-tla-cv-pipelining=false", ), (4, )),
+])
+def test_run(mix, single, extra, counts):
+    dtype = torch.float16 if mix else torch.float32
+    size = 256 if mix else 128
+    host = torch.arange(4 * size, dtype=dtype)
+    src = host.npu()
+    for count in counts:
+        dst = torch.full_like(src, -1)
+        staged_copy[(1, )](src, dst, count, MIX=mix, SINGLE=single, npuir_extra_options=extra)
+        expected = torch.full_like(host, -1)
+        expected[:count * size] = host[:count * size]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(dst.cpu(), expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

+    for dtype in DTYPES

+    B,

+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    L0_K: tl.constexpr,
+):

+    tl.static_assert(M % 16 == 0 and N % 16 == 0 and L0_K % 16 == 0)
+    tl.static_assert(K % L0_K == 0, "this example has no partial K tile")
+    tl.static_assert(2 * 2 * M * L0_K <= 64 * 1024)
+    tl.static_assert(2 * 2 * N * L0_K <= 64 * 1024)
+    tl.static_assert(4 * M * N <= 256 * 1024)
+    tl.static_assert(2 * K * (M + N) <= 512 * 1024)
+
+    with tla.scope.cube():
+        a_l1 = tla.alloc((K // 16, M // 16, 16, 16), A.dtype.element_ty, space="l1")
+        b_l1 = tla.alloc((N // 16, K // 16, 16, 16), B.dtype.element_ty, space="l1")
+        # Real separate allocations make slot identity visible. No proposed
+        # buffer-indexing API or implicit versions=2 scheduling is assumed.
+        a0 = tla.alloc((L0_K // 16, M // 16, 16, 16), A.dtype.element_ty, space="l0a")
+        a1 = tla.alloc((L0_K // 16, M // 16, 16, 16), A.dtype.element_ty, space="l0a")
+        b0 = tla.alloc((L0_K // 16, N // 16, 16, 16), B.dtype.element_ty, space="l0b")
+        b1 = tla.alloc((L0_K // 16, N // 16, 16, 16), B.dtype.element_ty, space="l0b")
+        acc = tla.alloc((N // 16, M // 16, 16, 16), tl.float32, space="l0c")

+        tla.load_gm_to_l1(tla.view(B, (K, N)), b_l1)

+        # returns exactly one M->MTE1 event for its own slot.

+                    k_part=L0_K,
+                    k_part_ceil=L0_K,
+                    k_part_loop=K // L0_K,
+                    k_part_actual=L0_K,
+                    m=M,

+            )
+            tla.copy_l1_to_l0(
+                b_l1,
+                b_tile,
+                tla.CopyL1ToL0Params(
+                    is_transpose=False,
+                    k_part_idx=ki,
+                    k_part=L0_K,
+                    k_part_ceil=L0_K,
+                    k_part_loop=K // L0_K,
+                    k_part_actual=L0_K,
+                    m=N,

+            tla.sync.wait_flag(tla.sync.PIPE.MTE1, tla.sync.PIPE.M, 0)

+                b_tile,
+                acc,

+                n=N,

+            tla.sync.set_flag(tla.sync.PIPE.M, tla.sync.PIPE.MTE1, ki % 2)

+        # K/L0_K == 1. Do not leak event state to later work on this core.
+        tla.sync.wait_flag(tla.sync.PIPE.M, tla.sync.PIPE.MTE1, 0)

+                unit_flag_ctrl=tla.UnitFlagMode.DISABLED,

+    b = torch.randn((case["K"], case["N"]), generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    x, y = a.npu(), b.npu()
+    out = torch.full((case["M"], case["N"]), float("nan"), dtype=torch.float32, device="npu")
+    # The kernel supplies cross-pipe synchronization explicitly.
+    options = dict(unit_flag=False, sync_solver=False)
+    if compile_only:

[TLA](fix) Align GM/UB DMA APIs with A5 support (#3279)

Expose LoadGM2UBParams.l2_cache_ctrl with L2CachePolicy.NORMAL_FV and
NORMAL_LV. Resolve omitted or None configuration explicitly to NORMAL_FV.
Keep existing member names and meanings stable as future L2 modes are added.
Bridge to the existing HIVM EvictFirst/EvictLast attributes; NPUIR retains
the hardware-value conversion. Remove the old public names and EvictNormal.

Remove all load_gm_to_ub padding configuration and native padding operands.
Document the intrinsic 32-byte alignment fill: Normal mode fills each burst,
while Ascend 950 Compact mode fills the combined region. Callers must reserve
and synchronize the full physical UB write footprint.

Remove StoreUB2GMParams, the store_ub_to_gm params argument and native
attribute forwarding. Adapt copy dispatch and DMA callers while preserving
independent set_atomic control and explicit reset. Delete unsupported
padding and per-store atomic test configurations without adding negatives.

Validation: matching wheel passed 5228 frontend/IR tests with 113 stage
skips and 32 DMA/copy tests on physical NPU0 (load/store 15, ND2NZ 15,
copy-only 2). Six direct-load/copy target-compilation and disassembly probes
confirmed None/NORMAL_FV/NORMAL_LV cache values 0/0/1; these extra probes
did not launch kernels. Cache hit rate and performance were not measured.

[TLA](fix) Add additional constraints (#3149)

* [TLA](fix) Enforce explicit resources for scalar conversions

Reject numeric fp64 conversions to narrower floating-point types in the
Python tla.cast frontend, including literal inputs and calls through JIT
helpers. Keep same-type casts and legal bitcasts, and retain the existing
BF16 source and destination restrictions at the scalar API boundary.

Cover the scalar type matrix, floating formats, rounding modes, FP64
literals and helper diagnostics without changing other TLA interfaces or
the shared adapter pipeline.

Validation: local scalar frontend checks passed in an isolated runtime
using an existing native build and compatible builder bindings. Python
syntax and git diff whitespace checks passed. No wheel rebuild, target
compilation or device execution was performed.

Assisted-by: AI
Signed-off-by: lbqg <songyaofei2@huawei.com>

* [TLA](fix) Reject scalar operations inside SIMD VFs

Reject select, abs, maximum, minimum, cast, cdiv and clamp inside SIMD
VFs, including literal inputs. Preserve max_value and infinity as typed
constant constructors allowed in either execution domain. Share the
execution-domain guard through scope.py for reuse by other TLA modules.

Record effective core and VF modes in the TLA caller context and carry
them into JIT helper specializations and callee initialization. SIMD
retains Vector ownership when a pure VV kernel omits the explicit Vector
scope. Restore the previous caller and builder contexts on scope exit.

Cover direct calls, helper reuse, control flow and constant exceptions.
Keep scalar clamp computation outside SIMD VFs.

Validation: 76 existing frontend contracts passed locally in an isolated
runtime using an existing native build and compatible builder bindings.
Python syntax and git diff whitespace checks passed. No wheel rebuild,
target compilation or device execution was performed.

Assisted-by: AI
Signed-off-by: lbqg <songyaofei2@huawei.com>

[TLA](feat) refactor copy&alloc_buffer&view&subview (#3224)

* [TLA](feat) refactor copy and alloc_buffer

Reapply #3143 on top of main-dev after its revert.

Remove the generic tla.copy dispatcher and the alloc_buffer alias;
callers use the explicit DMA route APIs (load_gm_to_ub,
store_ub_to_gm, load_gm_to_l1, ...) and tla.alloc with space=.

Assisted-by: AI

* [TLA](refactor) drop alloc versions and scope kwargs

Motivation: slim the alloc surface; versions and scope were redundant
spellings that can be expressed with existing public APIs.
Design: alloc now takes only shape/dtype/space. Multi-buffering is
requested explicitly via tla.annotate_buffer_versions(buf, n), which
emits the same hivm.multi_buffer annotation the old versions kwarg
forwarded to; N=1 remains a no-op. scope= callers switch to space=.
Tests updated accordingly, and the invalid-argument case now covers
annotate_buffer_versions directly.
Risks: behavioral parity is static (same callee, same value, same
emission point); error message wording changes slightly for the
positive-integer check.

Assisted-by: AI

* [TLA](feat) split view/subview roles and support dynamic dims

Motivation: tla.view previously accepted non-GM buffer sources while
subview only supported dynamic offsets. Users need a clear split (view
wraps GM kernel pointers only, subview slices buffers in any address
space) plus mixed static/dynamic sizes and strides end to end.

Design: view() now takes a scalar GM pointer only and forwards mixed
static/dynamic shape/strides/offsets through create_tla_pointer_view
(tt.make_tensor_ptr bridge, lowered to memref.reinterpret_cast), with
runtime row-major products as default strides. subview() lowers to
memref.subview with mixed OpFoldResult offsets/sizes/strides; dynamic
dims map to None in buffer_type and -1 in IR types. Remove the unused
create_tla_bind/create_tla_reinterpret_cast entries and the buffer
source path of view(); migrate the non-GM reshape case to subview and
align the frontend contract tests.

Risks: the C++ extension must be rebuilt; subview on GM buffers relies
on the bridge conversion without dedicated coverage.

Assisted-by: AI

* [TLA](test) migrate buffer view calls to subview, add dynamic UT

Motivation: after the view/subview role split, unittest still carried
the legacy buffer-source tla.view calls that the new frontend rejects,
and the dynamic-dimension capabilities plus subview-on-GM had no
dedicated coverage (flagged as a risk in the split commit).

Design: migrate all 22 buffer-source view calls in dsa_kernel.py plus
the expand.py UB row view to tla.subview with the new keyword
signature, and fix the stale positional subview call in reshape.py.
Add vector/view_dynamic.py, a 3-in-1 case covering runtime shape/
stride/offset on the GM pointer entry, subview on a GM view, and
dynamic pitched subview out of a UB allocation, each asserting the
mixed static/dynamic memref types and runtime operands at the IR stage
and exact-window accuracy at run stage. Extend view_frontend_contract
with GM-space preservation, dynamic-extent default strides, and
dynamic-entry bounds-check skip contracts.

Risks: IR/compile/run stages of the new tests were syntax-checked
only and still need execution on a Linux/NPU test machine.

Assisted-by: AI

* [TLA](refactor) rename annotate_buffer_versions to annotate_multi_buffer

Motivation: the old name required knowing that "buffer versions" means
multi-buffering; the new name states the intent directly and matches
the hivm.multi_buffer IR attribute it emits.
Design: mechanical rename of the definition, exports, docstrings and
all call sites in the TLA UTs; no behavior change.
Risks: None.

Assisted-by: AI

* [TLA] chore: fix yapf and clang-format violations

Motivation: files touched by the recent view/subview and rename commits
violated the repo yapf (column_limit=120) and clang-format rules, which
made the pre-commit hooks fail and block commits.
Design: run yapf -i on the affected Python files and clang-format -i on
tla_builder.cc; pure reformatting with no behavior change.
Risks: None.

Assisted-by: AI

+  stride and offset; ``tt.make_tensor_ptr`` must carry the runtime operands.
+- ``gm_subview``: ``tla.subview`` applied to a GM view (the buffer-space
+  bridge path) with runtime sizes and offset.
+- ``ub_dyn``: pitched ``tla.subview`` out of a UB allocation with runtime
+  sizes and offset.
+
+Dynamic entries map to ``?`` in the memref types and to runtime operands of
+``memref.subview`` / ``tt.make_tensor_ptr``. Run-stage launches vary ``rows``
+and ``off`` with values that share one specialization, so the runtime values
+must be honored rather than constant-folded.
+"""
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+
+import torch
+import triton.language as tl
+import triton.language.extra.tla as tla
+
+from utils.tla_test_utils import get_stages, compile_offline, lower_offline, check_lowered_ir, check_kernel_binary, matrix
+
+H, D, DPAD = 8, 128, 256
+
+CONFIGS = [
+    dict(name=f"{dtype}_{mode}", dtype=dtype, mode=mode)
+    for dtype in ("fp16", "bf16")
+    for mode in ("entry_dyn", "gm_subview", "ub_dyn")
+]
+DTYPES = {"fp16": (tl.float16, torch.float16), "bf16": (tl.bfloat16, torch.bfloat16)}
+
+
+def constants(case):
+    return dict(DTYPE=DTYPES[case["dtype"]][0], MODE=case["mode"], H=H, D=D, DPAD=DPAD)
+
+
+def signature(case):
+    return {"X": "*" + case["dtype"], "O": "*" + case["dtype"], "rows": "i32", "off": "i32", "pitch": "i32"}
+
+
+@tla.jit
+def dynamic_window(X, O, rows, off, pitch, DTYPE: tl.constexpr, MODE: tl.constexpr, H: tl.constexpr, D: tl.constexpr,
+                   DPAD: tl.constexpr):
+    with tla.scope.vector():
+        if MODE == "ub_dyn":
+            # Whole pitched tensor into UB, then a dynamic window out of it.
+            ub = tla.alloc((H, DPAD), DTYPE, space="ub")
+            tla.load_gm_to_ub(tla.view(X, (H, DPAD), strides=(pitch, 1)), ub)
+            tile = tla.subview(ub, offsets=(0, off), sizes=(rows, D))
+        else:
+            if MODE == "gm_subview":
+                # Slice the GM view itself: subview on a GM-space buffer.
+                base = tla.view(X, (H, DPAD), strides=(DPAD, 1))
+                src = tla.subview(base, offsets=(0, off), sizes=(rows, D))
+            else:  # entry_dyn: runtime shape, stride and offset on the entry.
+                src = tla.view(X, (rows, D), strides=(pitch, 1), offsets=(0, off))
+            ub = tla.alloc((H, D), DTYPE, space="ub")
+            tile = tla.subview(ub, offsets=(0, 0), sizes=(rows, D))
+            tla.load_gm_to_ub(src, tile)
+        tla.store_ub_to_gm(tile, tla.view(O, (rows, D), strides=(D, 1)))
+
+
+@matrix(CONFIGS)
+def test_ir(case, output_dir=None):
+    module, ctx = compile_offline(dynamic_window, signature(case), constants(case), output_dir=output_dir)
+    text = str(module)
+    assert "!tt.ptr" in text, "route A entry must keep pointer args at AST stage"
+    # Every mode routes exactly two GM pointer entries (source side + store side).
+    assert text.count("tt.make_tensor_ptr") == 2
+    assert text.count("tla.gm_view") == 2
+    assert text.count("memref.alloc()") == 1, "views must share one allocation"
+    if case["mode"] == "entry_dyn":
+        assert text.count("memref.subview") == 1
+        assert "strided<[?, 1], offset: ?>" in text, "runtime pitch must stay dynamic on the entry"
+    elif case["mode"] == "gm_subview":
+        assert text.count("memref.subview") == 2, "GM slice + UB tile carve"
+        assert "strided<[256, 1], offset: ?>" in text, "pitched GM subview result"
+        assert "strided<[128, 1], offset: ?>" in text, "UB tile carve result"
+    else:  # ub_dyn
+        assert text.count("memref.subview") == 1
+        assert "strided<[?, 1], offset: ?>" in text, "runtime pitch must stay dynamic on the entry"
+        assert "strided<[256, 1], offset: ?>" in text, "pitched UB subview result"
+    # Dynamic extents map to '?' in the memref types instead of specializing.
+    assert "memref<?x128x" in text
+    lowered = str(lower_offline(module, ctx, output_dir=output_dir))
+    check_lowered_ir(lowered, loads=1, stores=1)
+    assert "memref.reinterpret_cast" in lowered
+    print("IR PASS: view_dynamic", case["name"])
+
+
+def _launch(case, rows, off, compile_only=False):
+    dtype = DTYPES[case["dtype"]][1]
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(23)
+    x = torch.randint(-127, 128, (H, DPAD), generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    out = torch.full((rows, D), float("nan"), dtype=dtype, device="npu")
+    args = (x.npu(), out, rows, off, DPAD)
+    if compile_only:
+        return dynamic_window.warmup(*args, grid=(1, ), **constants(case)), None
+    kernel = dynamic_window[(1, )](*args, **constants(case))
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+    return kernel, out.cpu(), x[:rows, off:off + D].cpu()
+
+
+@matrix(CONFIGS)
+def test_compile(case):
+    kernel, _ = _launch(case, H, 0, compile_only=True)
+    check_kernel_binary(kernel)
+
+
+@matrix(CONFIGS)
+def test_run(case):
+    # (rows, off) pairs share one int specialization (none is 1 or %16==0
+    # except the offsets, which are all %16==0), so a single compiled kernel
+    # must honor the runtime values.
+    for rows, off in ((H, 0), (H, D), (H // 2, D)):
+        _, actual, expected = _launch(case, rows, off)
+        assert torch.equal(actual, expected), \
+            f"dynamic window addressed the wrong elements: rows={rows} off={off}"
+        print("ACCURACY PASS: view_dynamic", case["name"], f"rows={rows} off={off} exact window match")
+
+
+def main():
+    do_ir, do_compile, do_run = get_stages()
+    for case in CONFIGS:
+        if do_ir:
+            test_ir(case)
+        if do_compile:
+            test_compile(case)
+        if do_run:
+            test_run(case)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

[TLA](fix) Pass empty vcvt mode attr to VFTruncF/VFExtF (#3301)

* [build](chore) Update AscendNPU-IR submodule to stable e02c692a6

Motivation: triton-ascend should track the latest origin/stable tip of
AscendNPU-IR instead of a stale gitlink. The index pinned bd228faec while
the working tree had drifted to 1389120d7 (legacy-interface line), and both
predate the 11.19 stable sync.

Design: move the AscendNPU-IR gitlink to e02c692a6 (!5318 merge
sync1119/ab81b53f into stable), the current tip of origin/stable, which
supersedes the legacy-interface line.

Risks: the diff spans the 11.16 -> 11.19 stable syncs; libtriton must be
rebuilt against the new submodule and TLA offline IR re-validated.

Assisted-by: AI
Signed-off-by: liupengcheng2012 <liupengcheng38@huawei.com>

* [TLA](fix) Pass empty vcvt mode attr to VFTruncF/VFExtF

Motivation: the AscendNPU-IR stable bump to e02c692a6 pulled in 019bcd228
("support more vcvtff type conversions"), which appended
OptionalAttr<AVE_VCVT_ModeTypeAttr>:$mode to AVE_VFTruncFOp and
AVE_VFExtFOp. ODS emits optional attributes as positional create()
arguments without C++ defaults, so the two TLA builder call sites stopped
compiling ("requires 9 arguments, but 8 were provided").

Design: pass hivmave::VCVT_ModeTypeAttr{} (unset) at both call sites. TLA
already implements zeroing/merging through applySimdMode's vsel, and the
HIVMAVE-to-AVE lowering falls back to MERGING when the attribute is
absent, so the emitted code is unchanged.

Risks: None; the new attribute stays unset, matching the pre-bump behavior.

Assisted-by: AI
Signed-off-by: liupengcheng2012 <liupengcheng38@huawei.com>

* [CI](chore) Remove Build-Pinned-Wheels job from the Wheels workflow

Motivation: the job compiled AscendNPU-IR in-image on both x86_64 and
aarch64 (480-minute timeout each) to produce a verification wheel for the
pinned submodule revision, which is too expensive for PRs. Drop it along
with the plumbing that existed only for it: the pinned_wheel
workflow_dispatch input and the third_party/ascend/AscendNPU-IR path
trigger.

Design: delete the job block and its two inputs from ascend-wheels.yml.
Build-Wheels keeps tracking the AscendNPU-IR stable branch through the
prebuilt payload, and no other job consumed the pinned wheel artifact.

Risks: PRs that move the submodule pin no longer get an end-to-end wheel
bundling that exact revision; the pinned combination is still compiled by
the regular CI build jobs.

Assisted-by: AI
Signed-off-by: liupengcheng2012 <liupengcheng38@huawei.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: liupengcheng2012 <liupengcheng38@huawei.com>
Co-authored-by: liupengcheng2012 <liupengcheng38@huawei.com>
